stories.title: Podcast: How Landlords Can Solve the Tenant Visibility Problem – Sytes’ Rafael Weiss
stories.excerpt: Rafael Weiss is the co-founder of Sytes, a marketplace platform that connects commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively looking for space in real time. Rafael came to the problem as a developer who lost a deal because tenant demand was invisible until it was too late, and built Sytes to fix the information asymmetry at the core of retail leasing. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active site listings across all 50 states, with clients including Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, and Dutch Bros. Rafael is based in Boca Raton, Florida. (01:04) Retail’s Demand Visibility Problem (02:44) Why Sytes (04:04) A Filtration System for Tenant Demand (06:24) Getting First Customers to Pay Upfront (07:24) Why Tenant Demand Data Was Opaque (08:34) Anonymous Tenant Expansion (10:14) How a Deal Happens on Sytes (11:24) Church’s Chicken Case Study (14:54) Kimco & MyEyeDoctor Portfolio Review (16:34) REITs & Strip Centers (18:04) The Subscription Model (19:24) Retail Is Back (22:44) AI Leasing Agents & the Broker’s Future (24:04) Tenant Demand Index for Developers (27:24) Bootstrapping vs. Venture Capital Backing (28:24) Collaboration Superpower: Travis Kalanick Learn more: –Visit Sytes –Rafael Weiss on LinkedIn Virtual Events: –AI & Innovation Forum: Multifamily: on 9/29 –SFR / BTR Forum: on 10/22 In-person Events: –Institutional Investors & PE Forum: in NYC on 9/16 –South Florida Capital & Development Forum: in Miami on 10/15 –Finance Forum: in NYC on 11/3 –All upcoming Commercial Observer events Connect with Tangent: -Edward Cohen on LinkedIn -Zach Aarons on LinkedIn -Tangent on LinkedIn
bullets: Sytes platform connects 350+ tenants with 35,000+ listings across 50 states in real time
Solves retail leasing information asymmetry; clients include Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken
Enables tenant demand visibility for developers before deals close or markets shift
stories.summary: Rafael Weiss co-founded Sytes, a marketplace platform that gives landlords, developers, and brokers real-time visibility into active tenant demand across retail and commercial real estate. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active listings nationwide, with institutional clients including major REITs. Weiss built the company after losing a development deal because tenant interest remained hidden until too late, addressing a core market inefficiency in lease negotiation.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Sytes focuses on retail and commercial leasing transparency; however, the underlying insight—that hidden demand data creates missed value—applies broadly. A multifamily developer could use similar data-driven tenant-demand intelligence to time acquisitions and starts ahead of relocations or expansion signals in target markets, especially if such a platform expands into residential.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Scoops Up More Miami-Dade Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has bought two more affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County, following two acquisitions last week, bringing the total to $115.4 million and 570 units. The investment firm purchased the remaining piece of the Lafayette housing complex in Miami’s Little River neighborhood for $27 million, property records show. Called Lafayette Plaza, the 201,446-square-foot property houses 136 apartments at 155 Northeast 78th Street. The 14-story asset was completed on a 1.1-acre parcel in 2008. CBRE Capital Markets provided a $18.9 million loan, backed by Freddie Mac. Lafayette Plaza is attached to the 160-unit Lafayette Square building, which Starwood purchased for just under $30 million last week. In the second transaction this week, the Miami Beach-based firm purchased another property in Little River, Emerald Terrace, paying $24.6 million. CBRE Capital Markets once again supplied financing: a $17.2 million, Freddie Mac-backed loan. The complex, built in 2009 facing train tracks, houses 124 apartments and a 24,718-square-foot parking garage at 244 and 290 Northwest 72nd Terrace, near the retail center of the neighborhood, where popular restaurants such as Sunny’s Steakhouse are located. In the fourth acquisition, which closed last week, Starwood purchased the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments for $34 million. The 4.8-acre complex, built in 2011, features 20 three-story buildings near the southern end of the county in the Naranja neighborhood. Mansfield, Mass.-based Gatehouse Group developed and sold the four properties. CBRE’s Tim Flint, Jim Flinn and Jon Romano brokered all the recent sales and financings. A representative for Starwood confirmed the transactions. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management acquires 570 units, $115.4M total, four Miami-Dade properties in one week
Lafayette Plaza ($27M, 136 units) and Emerald Terrace ($24.6M, 124 units) purchased with Freddie Mac financing
Back-to-back affordable housing acquisitions signal strong institutional appetite in Little River submarket
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management closed four affordable housing acquisitions in Miami-Dade County totaling $115.4 million and 570 units within one week. The firm purchased Lafayette Plaza (136 units, $27M) and Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6M), both in Little River, financed by CBRE Capital Markets with Freddie Mac backing. Both loans were in the $17–$19 million range, allowing debt service on mid-2000s vintage assets.
stories.impact: Institutional capital rapidly consolidating affordable housing supply in Miami's Little River and adjacent neighborhoods. This signals confidence in Freddie Mac-backed multifamily underwriting and rental fundamentals in the submarket. For developers, this indicates strong rental demand supporting class-B/C asset valuations and Freddie Mac liquidity—a window to explore land or value-add opportunities in Little River and surrounding Miami-Dade neighborhoods before cap rates compress further on stabilized stock.

stories.title: Joint Venture Tops Off Construction on Mount Vernon Workforce Housing
stories.excerpt: City, county and state officials joined together to celebrate the topping off of QWest Towers, a new $158-million workforce housing development that is nearing completion in Mount Vernon, NY. Located at 1 and 25 North MacQuesten Pkwy., the project is being developed by QWest Towers LLC, a joint venture between Simone Development Companies and Stagg Group, in collaboration with the Rev. Dr. L’Judie Matt-Simmons. The 228-unit project consists of a 15-story tower and 12-story tower. The first tower will be completed later this year, with the second one to follow within a few months. Construction financing for the project includes support from New York State Housing and Community Renewal, Westchester County’s New Homes Land Acquisition program and the county’s Housing Flex Fund. The project also received financial incentives from the Mount Vernon Industrial Development Agency. ool District and the Mount Vernon Fire Department. bullets: QWest Towers joint venture (Simone Development, Stagg Group) topped off 228-unit workforce housing in Mount Vernon, NY

stories.summary: QWest Towers LLC, a joint venture of Simone Development Companies and Stagg Group, topped off a $158 million workforce housing development in Mount Vernon, NY, comprising 228 units across two towers (15 and 12 stories). The first tower will complete later in 2026, with the second following within months. Financing included New York State Housing and Community Renewal support, Westchester County land acquisition and Housing Flex funds, plus Mount Vernon IDA incentives.
stories.impact: Confirms strong public-sector support for workforce housing in suburban Westchester County, where labor and population pressure justify gap financing and tax incentives. For multifamily developers, this signals robust institutional (state/county) appetite for moderately priced rental in transit-accessible suburbs north of Manhattan. The project's size, structure, and multi-source funding model (state + county + IDA) is replicable for similar acquisitions or developments in Westchester and adjacent suburbs facing affordability and commuter demand.

stories.title: Skender Completes New Fulton Market HQ for Harrison Street Asset Management
stories.excerpt: Skender has completed the 83,000-square-foot buildout of Harrison Street Asset Management’s (HSAM) headquarters at The Fulton, 919 W. Fulton Market in Chicago. The real estate and infrastructure investment management firm is relocating from its prior location at 444 W. Lake Street. HSAM’s new three-floor buildout supports the need for a more flexible and functional workplace environment. Skender also served as the base building general contractor for the entire 535,000-square-foot development, which features several prominent office tenants in addition to Gibson’s Steakhouse and Equinox Fitness. Developed by Fulton Street Companies and the Shanna Collective, the property is the only Class A office building to break ground in Chicago since 2023. “We were so pleased to be able to assist Harrison Street Asset Management with their reimagined headquarters,” said Brian Eddy, senior project manager at Skender. “They now have a space that will inspire their people and support the organization long into the future.” The post Skender Completes New Fulton Market HQ for Harrison Street Asset Management appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Harrison Street Asset Management relocates HQ to 83,000-sf Fulton Market space, Chicago
The Fulton (535,000-sf) is Chicago's only Class A office to break ground since 2023; Skender was base GC and buildout contractor
HSAM move reflects demand for flexible, modern office despite headwinds; signals flight from older Loop space
stories.summary: Skender completed an 83,000-square-foot headquarters buildout for Harrison Street Asset Management (HSAM) at The Fulton, 919 W. Fulton Market in Chicago. HSAM relocated from its prior West Lake Street location to support flexible workplace needs. The Fulton, a 535,000-square-foot Class A office development by Fulton Street Companies and Shanna Collective, is Chicago's only Class A office to break ground since 2023 and houses Gibson's Steakhouse, Equinox Fitness, and other tenants.
stories.impact: HSAM's anchor lease validates Fulton Market's appeal to large institutional asset managers and signals ongoing demand for Class A office in Chicago's West Loop, despite broader office headwinds. For multifamily developers, this reinforces that mixed-use projects (office + retail + fitness) in walkable urban neighborhoods attract both corporate tenants and resident foot traffic, supporting residential lease rates. The rarity of new Class A office in Chicago since 2023 also underscores tight Grade-A supply, which may inflate office rents and make mixed-use development with residential components more attractive in core submarkets.

stories.title: Streamside RV Resorts Adds Maine Campground to National Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Streamside RV Resorts & Campgrounds, one of the fastest-growing owner-operators in the outdoor hospitality sector, today announced the acquisition of Sandy Pines Campground in Kennebunkport, ME. The transaction marks the 40th property in Streamside’s rapidly expanding national portfolio. The acquisition of the 46-acre coastal property was completed through a court-approved sale process. Located at 277 Mills Rd., Sandy Pines Campground features 224 total sites, including 83 RV sites, 46 tent sites, 66 glamping setups (including safari tents, A-frame hideaway huts, and glass houses), and 29 seasonal park models. “Our team has admired this property for some time, given the immense charm and draw of the Kennebunkport area,” said Jen Milam, Chief Growth Officer at Streamside. “Sandy Pines is a beautifully done resort in a fantastic location and has become one of the premier camping resorts in Maine. We are dedicated to preserving its deep ties to the local community, honoring its unique coastal character, and ensuring it remains a premier Northeast outdoor destination for generations to come.” The post Streamside RV Resorts Adds Maine Campground to National Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.

This competitive dynamic could inform mixed-use or experiential residential development strategies in coastal or leisure-destination submarkets, but does not directly signal multifamily demand, supply, capital, or cost shifts.

stories.title: Javits Center Expansion, Tech Upgrades Boosting NYC Hospitality Industry
stories.excerpt: Five years after the Javits Center underwent a $1.5 billion expansion, the Hudson Yards convention venue is continuing to expand its bandwidth to boost its events business and the adjacent New York City hospitality industry. The 3.3 million-square-foot facility recently underwent a $5 million technology upgrade enabling the Javits Center to become the first convention center in the U.S. to provide the newest wireless network, Wi-Fi 7, Commercial Observer can first report. The Wi-Fi 7 system, which debuted last month for Fanatics Fest, provides another competitive edge in attracting more conferences and events going forward, Joyce Leveston, CEO of the Javits Center, told CO. The original Jacob Javits Center opened in 1986. PHOTO: Edmund Vincent Gillon/Museum of the City of New York/Getty Images “So many people who are coming to conventions also want to feel that they can remotely connect with their workplace,” Leveston said on Wednesday, moments before the Javits Center marked its 40th anniversary with a celebration event. “You can’t do that unless you have a state-of-the-art Wi-Fi system.” The technology enhancement is just the latest effort by the Javits Center to up the ante in terms of drawing some of the biggest conferences and events to Manhattan and providing a jolt to New York City’s economy. The Javits Center estimates that its convention bookings generated more than 100,000 hotel stays in the New York City region in 2025. The expansion of the Javits Center, which debuted in May 2021, added 1.2 million square feet to the north side of the complex, including a 55,000-square-foot ballroom and a glass-enclosed sustainable rooftop pavilion touted as the largest green roof in the Northeast. The boost to New York City’s hospitality industry from new investments to the Javits Center is evident across the street at 418 11th Avenue, where a new 455-room Hilton-branded hotel is slated to open in the next three years as part of a larger mixed-use project. stories.impact: Javits expansion and Wi-Fi 7 deployment will increase event volume and occupancy in Hudson Yards, driving demand for nearby hotel and short-term rental supply. For multifamily developers in and around Hudson Yards and Chelsea, this signals sustained event-driven foot traffic and ancillary spending, supporting rents in mixed-use or hospitality-adjacent multifamily projects. The investment also reinforces NYC's infrastructure competitiveness, signaling institutional confidence in long-term tourism and convention demand recovery.

stories.title: Westphal Company Lands $56M Refi for San Diego Apartments
stories.excerpt: The Westphal Company has secured $56.1 million in permanent financing for a 354-unit apartment complex in eastern San Diego County. Northmarq arranged the fixed-rate financing through the firm’s Fannie Mae platform. The nonrecourse loan carries a 10-year term with interest-only payments for the full term. Property records identify Westphal Company owns the Wintercrest Village Apartments, a garden-style community at 12002 Wintercrest Drive in Lakeside, Calif., which is an unincorporated community roughly 20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego. The property features one- and two-bedroom apartments, along with two swimming pools and spas, outdoor courtyards, and fitness rooms. Northmarq’s Aaron Beck, Conor Freeman and Robbie Driscoll facilitated the financing, which allowed Westphal to extract equity from the property while maintaining its cash flow, according to Beck. The lender also waived all operating escrows. “With this Fannie Mae refinance, we were able to unlock trapped equity for the borrower and preserve cash flow while keeping the loan truly non-recourse with no carve-out guarantees,” Beck said in a statement. San Diego’s multifamily market stabilized in the second quarter, with vacancy holding at 5 percent and asking rents rising 0.5 percent to $2,598 per month, according to Northmarq’s second-quarter data. Investment sales slowed roughly 25 percent compared to last year, but median pricing jumped 25 percent to $415,000 per unit. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Westphal Company secured $56.1M Fannie Mae refi for Wintercrest Village Apartments, Lakeside, San Diego
354-unit garden-style property, 10-year fixed-rate nonrecourse, interest-only for full term, zero operating escrows
Northmarq facilitation; lender waived escrows, allowing equity extraction while preserving cash flow
stories.summary: The Westphal Company closed a $56.1 million permanent refinance through Northmarq's Fannie Mae platform for Wintercrest Village Apartments, a 354-unit garden-style community in Lakeside, California, 20 miles northeast of downtown San Diego. The 10-year fixed-rate nonrecourse loan features interest-only payments for the full term and waived operating escrows, allowing the borrower to extract equity while maintaining cash flow.
stories.impact: Fannie Mae liquidity and favorable underwriting (interest-only, no escrows, waived overlays) remain robust for stabilized multifamily in secondary San Diego County markets. This signals lender confidence in suburban San Diego rents and tenant quality. For developers, it confirms that Fannie Mae refi availability is a reliable exit strategy for value-add or stabilized garden-style assets in coastal California submarkets, supporting pro-forma underwriting and capital-stack assumptions.

stories.title: Fortress Refinances Dania Design Center With $45M After Foreclosure Fight
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, Fla., following a nasty foreclosure fight with its previous owner, New York-based billionaire Charles Cohen. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $45 million loan backing the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex at 1855 Griffin Road, facing the I-95. In the past two years, Fortress has invested about $3 million updating the campus, which dates back to 1988. Another $3 million to $5 million of renovations are planned over the coming year. In June, it tapped Jamestown to oversee management and leasing of the mixed-use property. The move comes about five years after the Design Center lost one of its main tenants, online pet retailer Chewy, which occupied about 100,000 square feet, when it relocated to Plantation Pointe. Fortress won control of Design Center and the neighboring Le Méridien Dania Beach hotel in 2024, through a $76 million credit bid. The proceeding was part of a broader foreclosure suit with Cohen Realty Enterprises, which Charles Cohen’s father Sherman Cohen had founded in the 1950s. In 2022, the New York-based lender provided a $535 million debt package, covering several commercial properties, including Cohens’s Dania Beach assets. The billionaire also personally guaranteed a $187 million portion of the loan. A year later, Cohen defaulted, prompting Fortress to take control of the commercial real estate. The lender also went after the borrower’s personal assets, believing the commercial properties were worth less than what Cohen owed, the Wall Street Journal reported. These include a chateau and vineyard estate in the south of France, a 220-foot megayacht, and a collection of Ferraris. In response, Cohen sold off several properties in New York. In June, Cohen announced that he had paid off the full judgement. But the legal battle remains, with Cohen filing to recoup $204 million in alleged damages. stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, Florida, with a $45 million loan from City National Bank of Florida, following a contentious foreclosure battle with prior owner Charles Cohen. The 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex, facing I-95, lost major tenant Chewy (100,000 sf) about five years ago. Fortress acquired control via a $76 million credit bid in 2024, invested $3 million in updates, and plans $3–5 million more renovations in 2026, having brought in Jamestown for management and leasing.
stories.impact: Fortress' refi and continued capex signal stabilization of the Design Center after distress, but the asset remains challenged by prior tenant loss and office headwinds. City National Bank's $45M loan reflects South Florida lender appetite for stabilized mixed-use office-showroom. For multifamily developers in South Florida, this underscores the risk of office-focused or design-sector tenancy in value-add assets; conversely, it may present acquisition or conversion opportunities if Fortress or similar operators refinance or divest underperforming office components in mixed-use buildings.
